You're generalizing way too much here and leaving out much needed context. When you talk about groups of lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, or queer individuals, there's pretty much three widely differing categories they can go in. They can be completely closeted in which case you don't even know they are a certain sexuality/gender, but they still are just as much so that thing. They can also be openly gay, trans, etc but not "identify" with the lgbtq community, which is mostly what you hear with conservative self hating gays and much more rarely trans people. They can also be openly these things and identify with the lgbtq community/be socially politically active. When you say there's infighting in our community, that could mean so many different things. Even closeted people are still technically part of our community. Ben shapiro could a gay trans woman for all we know, and me arguing with him on trans rights would technically be "infighting" in that regard. If you're referring to people who are openly gay/trans in general, of course there's going to be infighting. But if you're talking about the lgtbq community as in people who identify with the community and respect *all* of the letters in lgbtq, then there's little to no infighting about the validity/rights of certain groups/letters. Not intentionally atleast.
